summary: Crow's-nest cab atop an 86-foot pine, built early 1940s for railroad logging watch; abandoned 1958, the structure remains.

facts.design: Crow's-nest cab on top of an 86-foot pine tree, with a tent cabin for living quarters
facts.agency: Washington Department of Natural Resources - Division of Forestry

visit.trail_note: About three miles up an old logging road from a berm; 6.8 miles round trip with about 980 ft of gain; the route from the berm is a bit overgrown. The trail guide lists the land as private.

events.note: Panoramic photos taken from the cab top, July 14, 1941; the cab was standing by then. The register dates construction to the early 1940s.
Division of Forestry took ownership and fitted a fire finder and radio; a 1944 state report mentions a new lookout house at Meadow Butte
Dolores Coate stationed on Meadow Butte for the summer (Goldendale Sentinel, August 1948); a November 1948 article recalls Nancy Pearson's season four years earlier
Juanita Ward due to go on the lookout (Mt. Adams Sun)
Dorothy Lewis and Kathleen Ladiges staffed the lookout while Sylvia Anrig was away
Lookout abandoned; the structure still remains
DNR Southeast Region report: efforts to decide the future of the Meadow Butte ground cabin at Glenwood; building needs to move to a public place
Trail guide photos are from 2018 and describe the structure as still remaining

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, trail guide and Forest Lookouts page all describe a crow's-nest cab built on top of a pine tree, with a tent cabin for living quarters on the ground. The site is a tree cab, not a tower or a building.

notes_for_editor: Height is unresolved and no height_m is given: 86 ft (register, trail guide), 90 ft above ground (Forest Lookouts), 85 ft plus a 10 ft cab (WillhiteWeb), and an 80 ft ladder (1948 article). Land status conflicts: register says Washington State Lands; trail guide says private; firelookout page says Division of Forestry/DNR. Access level not recorded for that reason. Elevation: 3,607 ft (register), 3,621 ft (trail guide), 3,620 ft (fire lookout page); record's 1,099.4 m matches the register. Record's kind 'tree' and agency are confirmed. The 1948 spelling differs: Pearson in the article quote, Pierson in the trail guide's list. The 1944 'new lookout house' is unconfirmed as the base cabin. Current condition of the cab is not verified; the trail guide's photos are from 2018; a firelookout photo caption dated 2020 was seen only in a search summary, not in a fetched page. The Mt. Adams Sun and Goldendale Sentinel items are quoted secondhand via the Forest Lookouts page and not checked against originals. Photos (1940 and 1952 and 1979 by Ray Kresek; the 1941 panoramas) have no image URLs here, so none added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the August 18, 2018 visit date was removed (the trail guide page shows photos from 2018 but no such date); the Pearson/Pierson spellings and the Goldendale Sentinel date are now backed by the trail guide's own quotes; the route wording now matches the trail guide's 'a bit overgrown'.
